_comment: Junior Tennis Tour (src/systems/TourSystem.js, checked by `npm run validate` → validateTour). Hand-editable.
unlock.rafaWins: after-hours match wins over Coach Rafa (any difficulty) before he offers to coach you.

hank: npc id, rank = tour ranking at or better than this makes Hank ask 'play or take over my role', askAgainDays after 'Let me think'; the lines he says (ask / pro / grounds farewell / think / retired small talk on the grounds path).

careers: what each answer to Hank gives. pro: report-card title, gearDiscount (Jess's sponsorship on tennis gear, paid back at the till), sponsoredFees (the club pays entry fees; the Pro Circuit opens). grounds: title, wageMul and groomBonusMul (ShiftSystem multipliers; the data and Constants are never changed).
rafa: npc id and his offer lines (offer = multi-line dialogue, the last line gets the choices; session = the one line he says on the court).
ranking: best `bestOf` weekly results of the last `window` weeks (the current week included); ties by rating; unranked until the first points.

tiers: label; points per finishing round (W = title, F = runner-up, SF/QF/R16/R32 = lost in that round); prize ($ per finishing round, null = none); fee ($ to enter; the club pays it on the pro path); cutoff (the ranking you need to enter, null = open; home events always give the player a wildcard); formats per round ('short' = one set to 4, 'set' = one set to 6, 'bo3' = best of three); draws (draw sizes this tier may use: 8, 16 or 32); careers (who may enter: omit = everyone); juniors (pro tier: how many junior slots its draws keep, the rest are adults).

week: background event sizes per tier (the rest of the field plays these satellite events every week, simulated), backgroundPoints (their share of the tier points table), restChance (a player skips a week), jitter (how loosely players are sorted into events by ranking).

field: generated juniors (count, rating spread, ages), femaleShare (girls in the mixed field), weekly form spread, the surface preference bonus / weak-surface malus (rating points), rating drift per result (Elo K for the generated field) and the sim (serveBase = serve-point win chance between equal juniors, proServeBase for adults, k = logit per rating point).

venues: the six remote clubs (ids are fixed: the venues stream builds each from its `look`). look: court / surround / fenceColor / ground colours; fence 'chainlink' | 'windscreen' | 'hedge'; backdrop 'city' | 'forest' | 'harbor' | 'lawn' | 'campus' | 'night'; stands { rows, sides[], material?, covered? }; clubhouse { style 'shed' | 'lodge' | 'boathouse' | 'pavilion' | 'modern' | 'arena', color, roof, side, clock? }; trees { kind 'pine' | 'maple' | 'oak' | 'none', count, autumn? }; lights (floodlights); scoreboard?; sponsors (banner texts); crowd 0..1.
homeVenue: the club itself (the home event is played on the club's own court, no travel).

tournaments: the weekly rotation. circuit 'amateur' (default) rotates by weekSlot from the week you join the tour; circuit 'pro' events alternate with it once you choose the pro path. home: the club's own event (you always get a wildcard). wind overrides the venue's.

styles: play styles. sim = point-simulation edges (serve / return point chance, rating points per surface); ai = modifiers on Rafa's DIFFICULTY table for a tour opponent (a number adds, { mul } multiplies, { set } replaces; nested objects for serve / ret; arrays change every element); scout = the hub's scouting report.

names / clubs / shirtColors: pools for the generated players (firstM / firstF: first names by gender; a plain `first` list reads as they / them). clubJuniors: members of the club who play the tour (npc = npcs.json id, gender 'm' | 'f'). adults: the Pro Circuit's adult players (named ones are club members) plus `count` generated ones.
Texts about a player (scout lines, notes) write pronouns as tokens so they fit every opponent: {he} {him} {his} {he's} {himself} ({He} … at the start of a sentence).

offer: Three times you beat me. Three! After the second one I stopped pretending I was tired.
I have coached many juniors. You have something. You should play competitively: there is a Junior Tour, with tournaments at other clubs, real draws and a real ranking.
Let me be your coach. What do you say?
rafa.session: Three wins against me. Three! You should play competitively. Let me coach you.
accept: Vamos! Every week there is a tournament somewhere. You enter, you travel after your shift, you play under the lights.
Start with the local events. Win some matches, the ranking comes. I will be in your box.
later: Bueno. The offer stands. Come and find me when you are ready.
remind: The Junior Tour is still waiting for you. My offer stands.
So? Are you ready to play for real?

ask: Kid. Gloria showed me the junior rankings in the paper. Top ten. Top ten!
Here's the thing. I'm not getting any younger, and the board wants to know who takes over the grounds when I hang up the rake. I told them I know somebody.
But you've got a real shot at the tennis too. Can't do both properly. So what's it going to be?
pro: Then go and play. Properly. The club's putting its name behind you: your entry fees are on us from now on.
And Jess says she'll sponsor your gear. Twenty-five percent off the tennis wall. Don't make me watch you lose on the telly.
grounds: Here. The shed keys. The big one's the shed, the little one's the drag brush padlock, the green one... nobody knows. Keep it anyway.
The clay knows your hands now. Water it less than Rafa says and more than Frank says.
I'll still be around. Somebody's got to tell the Head Groundskeeper when the courts are too wet.
think: Take your time. Clay's not going anywhere. I'll ask you again in a few days.
retired: Morning, boss. Don't mind me. Just making sure you brush the lines last.
Retirement's great. I still wake up at five and smell the clay.
Gloria says I'm supervising. I'm not supervising. I'm observing. Loudly.
Court 4 looks good. Court 5... we'll talk.
Twenty-two years and I never once sat on this bench at noon. Nice bench.
You're doing fine, kid. Better than fine. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Frank still sends me the divot memos. I forward them to you now. That's retirement.
Still play on the tour? Good. The grounds can spare you for an evening.

homeVenue.name: Greenbriar Tennis & Social Club
homeVenue.blurb: Home. Your own Centre Court, your own members in the stands, and Hank's stripes on the grass.

venues.name: Cedar Park Public Courts
venues.blurb: City park courts: faded green paint, a chain-link cage, three rows of bleachers and apartment blocks behind the lights.

venues.name: Maple Hollow Racquet Club
venues.blurb: Red clay in a ring of maples, a white lodge clubhouse and wooden bleachers that creak on every big point.

venues.name: Harbor Point Tennis Center
venues.blurb: A blue hard court on the water, a boathouse clubhouse and pines bent by the sea wind. The toss never goes where you put it.

venues.name: Ashford Lawn Tennis Club
venues.blurb: The oldest lawn club in the county: a white timber pavilion with a clock, clipped hedges and a covered stand full of panama hats.

venues.name: Sunridge Tennis Academy
venues.blurb: A teal show court at the region's big academy: a glass training centre, a big two-sided stand and a proper scoreboard.

venues.name: Metro Tennis Center
venues.blurb: A night stadium downtown. Pro events only: twelve rows all round, a glowing scoreboard and the city skyline over the lights.

tournaments.name: Cedar Park Junior Open
tournaments.blurb: Where everybody starts: sixteen juniors, the city park and whoever brought a lawn chair.

tournaments.name: Maple Hollow Clay Classic
tournaments.blurb: Slow red clay and long rallies. Bring patience and spare socks.

tournaments.name: Harbor Point Junior Invitational
tournaments.blurb: A sea breeze across the court every evening: play with margin.

tournaments.name: Sunridge Academy Challenger
tournaments.blurb: Thirty-two juniors at the region's big academy, and every coach in the stand is scouting.

tournaments.name: Greenbriar Junior Open
tournaments.blurb: Your own club's event on Centre Court. The members will be watching, and you always get a wildcard.

tournaments.name: Ashford Lawn Junior Championships
tournaments.blurb: The grass-court nationals: low bounces, fast points and a very old trophy.

tournaments.name: Cedar Park Summer Slam
tournaments.blurb: An eight-player weekend shootout under the park lights.

tournaments.name: Maple Hollow Junior Nationals
tournaments.blurb: The clay-court nationals. The best juniors in the country, best-of-three final.

tournaments.name: Metro Tennis Center Open
tournaments.blurb: The Pro Circuit's night event downtown: adults, prize money and twelve rows of noise.

tournaments.name: Sunridge Pro Invitational
tournaments.blurb: Sixteen pros and a handful of juniors brave enough to play them.

baseliner.label: Baseliner
baseliner.blurb: Grinds from the back with deep, heavy groundstrokes.

strengths: Rarely misses from the back of the court
weaknesses: Short balls drag {him} out of {his} comfort zone
plan: Bring {him} forward: short slices and the odd drop shot
When {he} comes in, pass or lob {him}
Don't trade twenty-ball rallies from the baseline: change pace

counterpuncher.label: Counterpuncher
counterpuncher.blurb: Fast feet, gets everything back and waits for your mistake.

weaknesses: Can be pushed around by an aggressive first strike
plan: Be patient: build the point, don't go for the lines too early
Come forward behind deep approaches, {he} won't hurt you from far back
Take {his} second serve early and attack

bigServer.label: Big server
bigServer.blurb: Wins free points on serve and goes for everything.

strengths: Big forehand on the first ball after the serve
plan: Stand a step back on {his} first serve and just block it deep
Make {him} play one more ball: long rallies are yours
Move {him} side to side, {he} doesn't like running

serveVolleyer.label: Serve-and-volleyer
serveVolleyer.blurb: Serves and charges the net. Old school.

plan: Return low at {his} feet, {he} has to volley up
Pass {him} down the line, or lob when {he} crowds the net
Get your first serve in: {he} attacks second serves

moonballer.label: Moonballer
moonballer.blurb: Loops every ball high and deep and never gets bored.

weaknesses: Uncomfortable when you take the ball in the air
plan: Step in and take the high balls early, or volley them
Come to the net: {he} can't pass you with loops
Be patient, keep your own errors down

allCourt.label: All-court
allCourt.blurb: A bit of everything: rallies, comes in, slices, drops.

weaknesses: Can be pinned deep on the backhand
plan: Keep {him} back: deep balls stop {his} approaches
Serve wide and go for the open court

clubJuniors.note: Flat two-handed backhand and a serve {he} copied from Nate.
Ten years old and runs down every ball, occasionally the wrong one.

named.note: College captain, home for the summer. First-strike tennis: big serve, forehand, done.
